items.stem: Banks earn their core income primarily from:

options.text: The spread between interest earned on loans and paid on deposits
options.rationale: Correct: net interest spread is the core banking income.

options.text: Charging customers to store their exact banknotes
options.rationale: Banks lend deposits out; they do not simply store cash.
That is not the core income source.
Banks are not paid a government salary for operating.

items.explanation: Correct: net interest spread is the core banking income.

items.stem: Which two factors make a bank vulnerable to a liquidity crisis? (Select TWO)

options.rationale: Correct: maturity mismatch is a core liquidity vulnerability.

options.text: A sudden loss of depositor confidence
options.rationale: Correct: mass withdrawals can drain liquidity quickly.

options.text: Holding a large buffer of cash and liquid assets
options.rationale: That reduces, not raises, liquidity risk.
Profit does not prevent a short-term liquidity squeeze, but it is not the vulnerability itself.

items.explanation: Correct: maturity mismatch is a core liquidity vulnerability.

options.text: Reduce the incentive for depositors to run on a bank
options.rationale: Correct: insuring deposits calms depositors and curbs runs.

options.text: Guarantee the bank will always be profitable
options.rationale: It protects depositors, not bank profits.

options.text: Cover unlimited amounts for every account
options.rationale: Coverage is typically capped per depositor.

options.text: Replace the need for bank capital
options.rationale: Capital and insurance are complementary, not substitutes.
